newsitem.title: GERMANY: Low rise seen in German trucked air cargo in '97.
newsitem.headline: Low rise seen in German trucked air cargo in '97.

text.p: Trucked air freight is likely to show only small growth in Germany this year, one of the country's largest trucking companies said.
"In 1997 I see only a small market growth and falling prices," Hermann Schleinbecker, Frankfurt manager of Convent GmbH Air Cargo Road Transport, told Reuters.
This matched the moderate growth in air cargo flown to and from Germany this year, he added.
Schlienbecker said Convent had a share of 50-60 percent of the Frankfurt market for consolidated airfreight shipments.
"We do mostly consolidation business for airlines and forwarders serving nearly every airport in Germany. We are more of a national than an international trucker," he said.
The strongest routes were from Frankfurt to Hamburg, Munich, Nuremberg, Bremen and Hanover, he added.
Convent also operated to Amsterdam and ran occasional ad-hoc services to Brussels and Paris.
The trucker's main clients were Delta Air Lines for import business, United Airlines for imports and some exports and export trucking for American Airlines.
Other clients included Cathay Pacific, SAS Cargo and Brazilian carrier VASP, he added.
Convent is a family-owned company with offices at Emmerich, Frankfurt and Maastricht employing 110 staff and operating 55 trucks.
